subject: App gateway migration & SDK cutover plan
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>

Subject: App gateway migration & SDK cutover plan

Samir —

Thanks again for the sync earlier. Attached is a compact cutover plan and some SDK examples to help your eng team do a staged migration from your legacy gateway to our hosted endpoint. Core asks from our side: a sandbox cutover window, a single-eng contact for day-of, and confirmation of PO/contract timing so we can schedule reserved capacity.

High-level plan (proposed):
- Day 0 (sandbox): smoke tests + key rotation in sandbox (30–60m)
- Day 1 (pilot): 10% traffic routed to Redwood via gateway rule, 1-hour ramp
- Day 2 (cutover): full traffic shift, monitor 2 hours, rollback plan ready

Operational guidance included in attachments: migration-matrix.xlsx (mapping of endpoints + headers), sample-sdk-snippets.zip (node/python examples), cutover-checklist.md (day-of checklist).

Quick recommendations:
- Timeouts: 8s per synchronous request; for streaming endpoints use 60s socket/window timeout.
- Retries: exponential backoff with full jitter, max attempts = 5, initial = 200ms, cap = 10s.
- Rate limits: default policy is 100 req/min per API key; if you need higher throughput request a quota increase — we can issue a temporary burst policy during cutover.

Sample retry policy (Node.js pseudo):
const retryPolicy = {
  maxAttempts: 5,
  initialDelayMs: 200,
  maxDelayMs: 10000,
  jitter: true,
  retryOn: [429, 502, 503, 504] // do not retry 400/401/403
};

SDK init (Python snippet):
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="REDACTED", timeout=8)
# streaming: client = RedwoodClient(api_key=..., streaming_timeout=60)

Next steps: can you confirm sandbox cutover date and who will be the day-of eng contact? If procurement is still pending, loop Vivek for PO cadence.

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz

Samir —

Good questions — answers inline below and a few practical patches to the checklist so the eng team can run fast: 

1) Timeouts
- "8s per-request" means the HTTP client/request timeout. For long-running generation, set per-call socket/streaming timeout to 60s (or use streaming API which keeps the connection open). If you have endpoints that regularly exceed 8s, increase the request timeout for those calls or route them to a dedicated pool with larger sequence-length limits.

2) Idempotency and retries
- We recommend an idempotency key header (X-Redwood-Idempotency) on any call that triggers side effects (billing, downstream writes). Retry logic: only retry on idempotent-safe operations or when an idempotency key is present. Example policy: only retry POSTs with idempotency header; do not retry non-idempotent callbacks.

3) Rate limits and behavior on 429s
- During 429s our gateway returns 429 immediately (reject). We do not queue indefinitely. Best practice: exponential backoff + jitter client-side; implement a local token-bucket (leaky-bucket) to smooth spikes during the ramp. We can also provision a temporary burst quota for the cutover window — request this at least 48 hours before.

Cutover additions to checklist
- Validate idempotency headers in sandbox flows
- Run a synthetic traffic replay at 10%/minute to simulate ramp
- Confirm telemetry: token-level logs visible in Redwood Console (share dashboard link before cutover)

Example retry + idempotency (Node pseudo):
async function callWithRetry(payload, idempotencyKey) {
  let attempt = 0;
  while (attempt < 5) {
    try {
      return await client.call({ payload, headers: { 'X-Redwood-Idempotency': idempotencyKey } });
    } catch (err) {
      if (![429, 502, 503, 504].includes(err.status) || attempt === 4) throw err;
      const delay = Math.min(10000, 200 * Math.pow(2, attempt));
      await sleep(delay + jitter());
      attempt++;
    }
  }
}

Sandboxes and testing
- Sandbox endpoint: https://sandbox.redwood.ai/clearpay — this mirrors production rate limits by default but we can relax them on request for test windows.

Support during pilot
- Day-of primary: Vanessa Ortiz (day-of coordination)
- Escalation: Vivek Kulkarni (billing / PO / capacity raises) — vivek will also open a short Slack channel with your eng lead.

I'll update the cutover-checklist.md with idempotency items and the synthetic replay steps. Confirm sandbox window and eng contact and we'll lock calendar invites.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
